verdict.headline: Mandatory Penalty Kick Omitted
verdict.subheadline: Violation of IFAB Law 12.1 & Direct Breach of 2024 Tyrone Mings UEFA Precedent
broadcastTakeaway: The goal-kick restart was legally complete the moment goalkeeper Musso kicked and clearly moved the ball.
Defender Marc Pubill deliberately picked up the live ball with both hands inside the 18-yard box to reposition it.
Under IFAB Law 12.1 and binding UEFA directives, handling a live ball inside the penalty box mandates a penalty kick and a second yellow card.

contactPoint.description: Deliberate two-hand pickup on live ball

deliberation.message: Advocate Position: Defend on-field call. Referee Kovács had an unobstructed direct sightline (22m distance). Contact occurred during an unpressured defensive restart with no active attacking phase, supporting the high Clear & Obvious threshold for non-intervention.

Audit Objection: IFAB Law 16.1 explicitly dictates 'The ball is in play when it is kicked and clearly moves.' Once Musso kicked the ball, the restart was consummated. Law 12.1 categorizes deliberate hand contact in the box as an objective, non-interpretative penalty offense. In Club Brugge vs Aston Villa (2024), referee Stieler awarded a penalty against Tyrone Mings under identical spatial mechanics.

Arbitration Finding: Overturn warranted. The Clear & Obvious threshold was breached because the handling was deliberate, unambiguous, and occurred on a live ball. 98.4% statistical parity with the Mings precedent dictates a mandatory penalty kick. Precedent Deviation Index: 92%.

precedent.title: Aston Villa vs. Club Brugge
precedent.officialRuling: Penalty Kick Awarded (Confirmed by UEFA Technical Committee)
precedent.deviationAnalysis: In both instances, the goalkeeper took a short lateral goal kick to a defender who picked up the moving ball with his hands under the false impression play had not restarted. While Mings was penalized, Pubill was granted immunity, representing an acute 92% inter-match consistency divergence.

verbatimStatutes.text: The ball must be stationary and is kicked from any point within the goal area by a player of the defending team. The ball is in play when it is kicked and clearly moves.

verbatimStatutes.subclause: Fouls and Misconduct: Handling the ball
verbatimStatutes.text: It is an offence if a player deliberately touches the ball with their hand/arm, for example moving the hand/arm towards the ball. A penalty kick is awarded if an offense occurs inside the penalty area.
